preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract deployer/owner
Contract must not have been initialized yet (fresh deployment)

violation_target.exploit_hint: The contract uses a constructor instead of an initializer function, making it vulnerable to front-running attacks. As the deployer, call the constructor with malicious parameters (e.g., set token address to attacker-controlled token, set subsequentClaim to 100e18 for instant 100% claims). This allows unauthorized initialization of critical contract parameters.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract uses a constructor to initialize critical parameters (token address, subsequentClaim percentage, claimPeriod). If deployed with malicious parameters (e.g., subsequentClaim = 100e18 meaning 100% per period), an attacker who is also the owner can add themselves as a distribution wallet and immediately claim all tokens. The constructor is only called once during deployment, so this vulnerability exists from the moment of deployment and cannot be fixed without redeploying.
attempts.attack_strategy: Deploy a new instance of the Advisory contract with malicious parameters: set subsequentClaim to 100e18 (100%) so we can claim everything in one period. Then as owner, add ourselves as a distribution wallet with a large balance, and immediately claim all tokens.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy a malicious ERC20 token we control. 2. Deploy Advisory contract with our token address and subsequentClaim = 100e18 (100%). 3. Mint tokens to the Advisory contract. 4. As owner, add attacker address as distribution wallet with all tokens. 5. Wait for claim period (or set startTime in future and warp). 6. Call claim() to get all tokens immediately.
